subject: general
question: What type of forest underwent a remarkable recovery with the active and willing participation of the local community in the Arabari forest range of Midnapore district?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sal forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1972, the** West Bengal Forest Department** admitted its failure to **revive the state's degraded Sal forests** in the southwestern regions.
 
• **Traditional surveillance** and **enforcement practices** had resulted in a **"complete alienation of the people from the administration"**, resulting in frequent conflicts between forest officials and villagers.
 
• The region's forest and land disputes also contributed significantly to the Naxalites' militant peasant activities.
 
• As a result, the Department shifted its strategy making a beginning in the** Arabari forest range of the Midnapore district**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sandalwood forests:**

 
 
• ​Due to India's historical contribution of **85% of the global sandalwood trade**, sandalwood has long been associated with Indian heritage and culture.
 
• But lately, this has been **rapidly decreasing**.
 
• It is also known as **"Chandan" and "Srigandha"** in India.
 
• From the newborn to the **cremation**, sandalwood is used extensively in Indian culture.
 
• It is** primarily grown** in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Bihar, Gujarat, Karnataka, M.P., and Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Teak forests (Sagwan):**
 
 
• A species of tropical hardwood tree belonging to the Lamiaceae family is teak.
 
• In mixed hardwood woods, it is a sizable **deciduous tree**.
 
• Teak trees have big, papery leaves that are frequently hairy on the underside.
 
• Freshly milled teak wood **smells like leather** and is highly prized for its toughness and water resistance.
 
• Teak is found in Nilambur teak, Adilabad teak, Godhavari teak, Konni Teak, etc. 
 
 
 
• **Neem forests:**
 
 
• One of the most beneficial and** priceless tree species** found in India is the neem (Azadirachta indica), a member of the meliaceae family.
 
• Its ability to grow in a variety of soils up to a pH of 10 makes it one of the most useful and significant trees in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is **found all over India** and can thrive in all agroclimatic zones, with the exception of high and cold regions and dam sites.
